title: Mage Knight
observed_goal: In the menu frame, suggested goals/modes include entering the dungeon, co-op, arena, and versus; in the active gameplay frames, wave 1 of 10 and a boss counter of 0 of 5 are displayed. The final goal, victory, or level completion was not observed.
observed_controls: In the on-page guide text: hold LMB to aim, F for magic, link the basic spell and magic with Link, and Space to dodge.
In the gameplay-frame HUD: movement with W/A/S/D and pause with Esc are displayed.
The metadata records attempts with the inputs Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and holding ArrowRight + Space for 900 milliseconds; acceptance of these inputs was not independently confirmed.
observed_core_loop: In the active gameplay frames, a character is visible in a movement-oriented arena with enemies/targets, a health bar, wave, boss, time, chain, and ability cards. Across the after_key_burst, after_combined_input, and late frames, the state and positions of elements change and more enemies/indicators are visible, but these changes alone do not establish a repeatable loop, input causality, or a complete outcome.
progress_feedback: The gameplay frames show an explicit HUD for level 1, 5 hearts of health, chain 0, mastery grade D, wave 1/10, boss 0/5, time 00:00 to 00:01, and ability bars/cards. No increase in wave, score, level progression, or event completion was observed.
decisions_risk_reward: The menu shows several rows of selectable abilities/spells and the possible use of aiming, magic, and dodging on the page. Actual decision-making, risk/reward, resource consumption, or the effects of choices were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive in the recorded run.
rewards: Several selectable abilities/spells are visible in the menu, and relics and ability cards are visible in the HUD; reward acquisition, upgrades, or reward effects were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive in the recorded run.
penalties_failure: Health and boss indicators are visible in the HUD, but damage, failure, loss of a life, a penalty, or a loss screen was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
outcomes_replay: An outcome, victory, loss, wave completion, replay, or complete repeat loop was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
onboarding: After loading at 0%, the after_start frame shows a readable menu with basic/dash/secondary/ultimate selections and game-mode buttons. A control guide is also present in the HUD. Step-by-step onboarding or confirmation of how the user enters the loop from the menu was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: The frames show a pixel interface with high contrast, text labels, icons, status bars, and HUD elements. Audio, accessibility settings, subtitles, color-blind support, or input remapping was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The page has a canvas with dimensions 1280×800, and the metadata records four script, thirteen fetch, one xhr, and one image; this is only a technical clue and does not establish the game architecture.
The page log records Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official and execution with WebGL 2.0 / OpenGL ES 3.0 using Emscripten 4.0.20; this technical clue concerns the runtime technology, not game logic.

Changes between frames after inputs may be caused by animation or the passage of time; the metadata explicitly states that input acceptance was not established and that no tuning constant or engine marker was recorded.

Several 403 errors and a remote config error were recorded in the console, but no request failure or page error was recorded; their effect on the game experience was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
transferable_principles: A compact HUD can make health status, stage progress, time, and ready abilities readable at the same time; this should be validated through interaction and outcome testing.
Separating ability selection from the playfield clarifies the initial choice and allows options to be compared before entering action.
Displaying ability readiness and the main controls in the same gameplay frame reduces the cost of shifting the user’s attention.
To establish an action loop, continuous input logging, attributable state change, and consequence must be recorded separately; a change in the image alone is insufficient.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, the principle of a readable HUD and state feedback can be tested only in the abstract; score/rank should solely reflect skill.
No gameplay advantage should depend on a purchase or wallet.
free brake and horizontal direction change should not be proposed as definitive solutions; a branching path requiring a new control is likewise only a hypothesis requiring testing.

The only reliably transferable part of this evidence is the organization of feedback and display of existing controls; mapping mechanics or a functional outcome was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce this game’s name, character, art direction, environment, text, sound, brand, or asset.
Do not use the official card’s claim about magic chain, dodging, or multiplayer modes as confirmed mechanics; their complete execution was not recorded.
Do not treat changes in enemy or character positions between frames alone as evidence of input acceptance or mechanic success.
Avoid conclusions about victory, loss, rewards, penalties, or a repeatable loop without an outcome-bearing frame.

evidence.claim: The page proceeds from a loading screen titled Mage Knight at 0% to a selection menu.
The menu shows rows for selecting abilities/spells and options to enter the dungeon, co-op, arena, and versus.
On the active gameplay page, health, level, chain, mastery grade, wave, bosses, time, and ability cards are displayed.
The HUD text states the controls LMB, F, Link, and Space for dodge, and W/A/S/D for movement and Esc for pause.
The after_combined_input and late frames show changes in character/enemy positions and time from 00:00 to 00:01, but these changes do not establish input acceptance.
The official card claim describes building an arsenal from seven elements, magic chain, timed dodging, arena, co-op, and online duels; this claim was not playtested against the recorded execution.
The technical log records Godot, WebGL 2.0, and Emscripten, and the metadata shows the absence of a tuning constant and engine marker.
The metadata states that image changes may be animation or the passage of time and that the generic input sequence is not a game-specific playtest.

limitations: This analysis relies only on evidence.json and five local frames of this game; no web browsing or speculation about hidden controls was performed. The official card is reported solely as a claim and is not a complete playtest. The frames provide direct evidence of active gameplay, but do not show a repeatable loop, input causality, outcome, victory, or loss; therefore, the related fields have been kept as “not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive” wherever necessary.
